title: THE MIND OF A CHILD: VOID OF EGO AND PRIDE

sense.text:
This is the wisdom for the week: don’t be a stupid person. The seven signs of a stupid person are a constant need to be right, blaming others for everything, talking more than listening, refusing to learn and to take advice, overconfidence without substance, judging others too quickly, and being the perpetual complainer who sees a problem and brings no solution. Some of these things were in all of us when we were young in the truth. If you fall into any of them, you can fix it.

These classes are for examination and for healing. A smart person sees a problem and comes up with a solution; a stupid person sees a problem and complains. A brother or sister who is given counsel according to the scriptures and won’t follow it is a stupid person: counsel is given twice on the same matter, and if you don’t follow it, don’t come back. And don’t be quick to judge. Judging a brother on what one person brought, without hearing his side, makes you look stupid, because people misunderstand and people lie. Judge nothing without two or three witnesses, and don’t counsel a husband or wife alone; hear both of them.

“The law of the Lord is perfect”: God’s laws are perfect. “Converting the soul”: they change you. “The testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” The simple are stupid people. God’s laws change stupid people. If you want to change, if you want to stop being stupid, apply God’s laws to your life, and the law of the Lord will make wise the simple.

precepts.why:
“The way of a fool is right in his own eyes.” If you are a fool, if you are stupid, whatever you do is always right in your own eyes. That is the first sign of a stupid person: you are always right. Everybody else is telling you that you are wrong, but in your eyes you are right. The way of a stupid person is right in his own eyes.

“But he that hearkeneth unto counsel is wise.” If you can take advice, if you can take correction, you are wise. That is what makes you wise, and that is how God’s laws convert you. If you can take criticism, even from your spouse, you are wise. Sisters, your husband is going to tell you things you are doing that aren’t right. All you have to do is listen. Don’t fight against it; fighting it is what makes you stupid. The wise listen and take counsel.

“A prudent man concealeth knowledge: but the heart of fools proclaimeth foolishness.” If you are a fool, you are just going to talk foolishness, because your heart is full of foolishness. That foolishness is those seven signs: you don’t want to take correction, you don’t want to listen to anyone, you are arrogant.

“Whoso loveth instruction loveth knowledge”: if you love to be instructed, you love knowledge. “But he that hateth reproof is brutish.” If you don’t like to be corrected, if you hate it when somebody tells you that what you did was wrong, the scripture says you are brutish. Brutish is stupid.

Here is somebody trying to help you. You know you are doing something wrong, they tell you to stop, and you hate them for pointing out your fault. That is a stupid person.

“Sand, and salt, and a mass of iron, is easier to bear, than a man without understanding.” Back in the day they carried sand and salt in bags, and that is very heavy. A mass of iron is heavy too. Yet it is easier to bear these heavy burdens than to deal with a man without understanding, somebody that is a damn fool, that is stupid.

Why? Because a stupid person will argue with you all the time, will never take the wrong for what he did, and will always cause confusion. So don’t be stupid. And if you are stupid, God’s law is going to fix you: it will convert you and make you wise.

sense.text:
“Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me, declaring the end from the beginning.” The Lord declared the end, and the time we are living in right now is the end, but he declared it from the beginning, “and from ancient times”: the time of Moses, Abraham and Adam. He let us know “the things that are not yet done”. He wrote it down; he let the prophets know what was going to happen.

“Saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure”: what God said shall stand. So everything we see happening in the world today, Russia and Ukraine, the earthquakes all over the world, Iran and America, Yemen and Saudi Arabia, Lebanon, Palestine, God declared all of it from the beginning. It is amazing to see these things come to pass, and it builds your faith up: this Bible is a real book.

This week the Houthis in Yemen, whom the western world calls rebels but whom the people there call revolutionaries, routed the Saudi-backed forces and took the Bab el-Mandeb strait, through which the trade from the Suez Canal must pass. Hormuz was already choked off by Iran; now this waterway is shut too. Oil is climbing, fertilizer will be cut off, and that means famine. The Bible calls this the beginning of sorrows. The Lord is behind all of this, and it is going to get worse and worse. Don’t sit and wait for things to get better: prepare. We need our own food supply, our own water. The dragons of Arabia are waking up.

“The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see.” The burden is the destruction, the judgment God is going to bring on Babylon, and Isaiah saw it. This Babylon is not only ancient Babylon. It is the Babylon of today, Mystery Babylon, America.

“Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them.” The Medes are the Persians, and that is Iran today. The same way the ancient Medes and Persians were raised up to destroy ancient Babylon, God is using modern-day Media and Persia, Iran, to weaken and to play a role in destroying Mystery Babylon. History is repeating itself. God says, I will raise up Iran against America.

“Which shall not regard silver; and as for gold, they shall not delight in it.” You can’t pay them off. Trump offered them money; Iran doesn’t care about money. Saudi Arabia cares about money. America went over there and killed the Ayatollah, his wife and his kids, and now what goes through the mind of those people is vengeance: their whole mission is to destroy Babylon.

Iran is fighting with asymmetric warfare, where the weaker side uses unconventional tactics to exploit the stronger side’s weaknesses, weakening America’s economy and dividing her politicians. That is the same way Cyrus took ancient Babylon: not by a costly frontal assault but from within. The Most High is behind it. The pride of Trump’s heart has deceived him, and America has woken up the dragons of Arabia.

“Their bows also shall dash the young men to pieces.” Their bows are their missiles, ballistic missiles. That is why Iran is so good at making them: it is according to the prophecy. “And they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eye shall not spare children.” This is going into Armageddon; this is when Iran gets their payback.

“And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms”: that is America, Mystery Babylon. She “shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah with fire and brimstone, so this shows that Iran will eventually acquire nuclear capability. This is the Babylon in the future that Isaiah saw being destroyed, and Iran, the Medes, has a big role to play in it.

“It shall never be inhabited, neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation.” Ancient Babylon was still inhabited after Cyrus conquered it, so we know this is not talking about ancient Babylon. It is talking about Mystery Babylon, where we are living. America will never be inhabited again after that destruction.

When Isaiah wrote this, he did not divide it into chapters; it was one continual vision. Chapter 14 is a continuation of chapter 13, the same chain of thought concerning Babylon. So after Babylon is destroyed, “the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel”: he is going to choose us, “and set them in their own land”: he is going to put us back in our land. “And the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob”: they are going to be our servants.

“And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place”: everybody is going back to their own land. “And the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids”: all nations are going to serve us, after Babylon is destroyed. “And they shall take them captives, whose captives they were.” Are we captives here in America? Yes, we are. “And they shall rule over their oppressors”: after Babylon is destroyed, we are going to rule over our oppressors.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve.” Isaiah saw us at rest, delivered out of here, in the kingdom, ruling the earth in righteousness. “That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon”: the same Babylon of chapter 13. Those of us that make it are going to take up a proverb against America.

“And say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” We are not asking how America was destroyed; we are making a statement. Isaiah sees us in the kingdom talking among our servants, and from here he explains how the oppressor ceased, how the golden city was destroyed.

“The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers.” We are the ones saying this. “He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke, he that ruled the nations in anger”: that is what America did. He “is persecuted, and none hindereth.” When he is destroyed, “the whole earth is at rest, and is quiet: they break forth into singing. Yea, the fir trees rejoice at thee.” America is already destroyed in chapter 13; now Isaiah is explaining how.

Chapter 13 said God would stir up the Medes; here Isaiah goes deeper. “Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming: it stirreth up the dead for thee, even all the chief ones of the earth; it hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.” All the leaders of the earth will be stirred up to come against America.

Why? Because of what America is doing now. America assassinated the Iranian leaders, and the war she started will throw the world into a financial collapse. The nations will hate her for it; Europe will hate her, because that war is going to hit Europe very badly. Europe supported America in all the evil she did from 1945 until Trump came into office, disrespected them and put tariffs on them.

“All they shall speak and say unto thee, Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us?” Before America is destroyed, she will become weak, economically and militarily. She will lose the world’s economic power and her military dominance, the nations will see it, and that is why they will rise up and come against her. This is the beginning stage of America’s decline, and Iran, the Medes of the chapter before, is playing a role in it.

“Thy pomp is brought down to the grave, and the noise of thy viols: the worm is spread under thee, and the worms cover thee. How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer”: Lucifer is the king of Babylon in the verses above. Isaiah is showing how Lucifer is going to fall from heaven: the nations will rise up against her.

“That made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof”: America made the world a wilderness. This is why she fell: she was destroying nations, making nations a wilderness, and the kings of the earth saw her become weak and rose up against her.

“All the kings of the nations, even all of them, lie in glory, every one in his own house. But thou art cast out of thy grave like an abominable branch.” America is already destroyed here; Isaiah 14 is going into why and how. Read on and Isaiah speaks of Palestina, letting you know what caused America to be destroyed: what America and Israel are doing over there in Palestine, in Lebanon, in Yemen and Saudi Arabia.

Iran is doing today what was done to take down ancient Babylon. The Saudi leaders care only about money, not their people; their people will rise up and get rid of them, and the Arabs will unify. Under the petrodollar deal of 1973 America promised Saudi Arabia military protection in return for oil sold only in dollars. Now Saudi Arabia calls for help and America tells them they are on their own. Iran is showing the Arabs that the West does not care about them. You storing up riches in the bank: this world is coming to an end. Get your mind right.

“Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?” The disciples came asking who was going to be the greatest. That was not the right spirit they were rolling in. What they were really saying was, I am going to be better than you. That is ego and pride, and they didn’t know it. So Christ had to correct them and check them: you can’t think like that.

“And Jesus called a little child unto him, and set him in the midst of them”, and said, “Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.”

What are the characteristics of a little child? A little child has to be guided. A little child doesn’t have ego and pride. When a child is very young, he listens: you tell him to get over there, to do this, to do that, and he does it. As children grow older they start to develop these demons, pride and ego. A child also forgives easily, and a child doesn’t deal with fear.

There are two forms of ego and pride. There is good pride: I am proud to be an Israelite, proud that the Lord called me into this truth. Everybody has an ego, and you have to control it, because it can be used in a good way or a bad way. Ego and pride go hand in hand; when the Bible talks about pride, a lot of the time it is going into ego, into being egotistical. The bad pride is superiority and arrogance: thinking you are better and greater than others, nobody can say anything to you, you don’t listen to anybody. That is the pride and the ego God doesn’t like.

“Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.” Christ didn’t pick any of them and say, you will be the greatest. He said whoever humbles himself and becomes like this little child, that one is the greatest. We must become as little children and humble ourselves as little children to get the kingdom of heaven.

precepts.why:
Pride, arrogance, ego: you are not going to find these in the mind of a child. They develop in you over time, and they come out of the heart: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye”, that is jealousy, “blasphemy, pride”.

That pride goes into arrogance. It goes into not wanting to take correction. It goes into ego: you are egotistical, nobody can say anything to you, you think you are better than everyone.

The signs of pride in you that you may not know: always wanting to win or be first, which was on the apostles, but they corrected it; talking a lot about yourself, me, me, me, being self-absorbed, always on your damn phone taking selfies; not admitting when you are wrong, because your ego won’t allow it; thinking you are better than others, I’m a better teacher than you, I can break down the scripture better than you, and the Lord reads your mind and sees it; being unwilling to learn from others; acting like the rules don’t apply to you, when the rules apply to everybody, the deacon included; ignoring or dismissing other people’s ideas; making fun of others; refusing to help or work together with others; and being overly focused on your appearance or status. When the restructuring was done and some brothers were taken down from officer of 50 to officer of 10, some gave up their rank altogether. That is pride: they wanted to be over brothers and were not here sincerely. And sisters, nobody was made to be over anyone; your job is to set an example and help the sisters.

“If any man desire to be first, the same shall be last of all, and servant of all.” If you want to be great, if you want to be first, you have to be last, and to be last you have to become a servant. Christ isn’t looking for brothers to come up in here puffing up their chest. That is what real leaders do: their job is to help the people, not to put themselves up.

“Fulfil ye my joy, that ye be likeminded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind.” One of the spirits of pride is not being able to work together; we must be likeminded, of one accord and of one mind.

“Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory.” Vainglory is doing things to be seen, getting glory from men, which is vain. A brother does a good lesson that helps a lot of people, the people thank him, and it gets to his head. He becomes full of himself and starts loving it, saying, you don’t know how many hours I put into that, instead of saying all praises to the Lord. When a lesson is taught it is the Lord speaking; that feeling you get is the Spirit of Christ. There is no glory in the man teaching. We are all unprofitable servants.

“But in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.” In lowliness of mind means you must humble yourself. To esteem others better than yourself, you have to see the qualities in your brother and appreciate them. Paul says this because Christ taught it to them in Matthew 18, when they asked who would be greatest. Esteeming the next person better than you takes away the ego, and that spirit won’t jump on you. Always give the Lord the honor and the glory for anything you do in this truth, because he is behind everything we do.

“Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others”: care about others. That is what real leaders do, and what we all have to train ourselves to do. “Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus”: that is the mind we have to have.

“Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.” Part of pride is not wanting to take correction and not accepting when you are wrong. When you are wrong, you have to be able to confess that you are wrong and get rid of the prideful spirit. That is the only way healing can come into that relationship.

“I wrote unto the church: but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.” Preeminence is pride and ego: thinking you are better than everybody. That is how Diotrephes was rolling: to hell with the apostles, don’t let them in here, this is my church. “Wherefore, if I come, I will remember his deeds which he doeth, prating against us with malicious words”: he was talking crazy about the apostles.

That spirit should not be on brothers. If you get it, you have to shake it off. You may hide it from us, but God knows what is inside you. If you desire preeminence, fame and glory, and that is why you want to be a leader, you are not going to last long in this truth.

“Let us not be desirous of vain glory”: the glory of men, people praising you. Give the Lord the praise; don’t take it for yourself. “Provoking one another”: when you roll in that spirit, I’m better than you, I’m a better teacher than you, you provoke one another. “Envying one another”: and then envy rises up, and brothers start envying each other. The vainglory spirit is the brother who wants to be better than everyone.
“Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly.” All of these scriptures are going into one thing: not having a freaking ego and not having pride.

“And upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them.” An oration is a speech. “And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.” Herod could speak very well, and they said this man is a god.

“And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him.” God killed him right there. He knew better; he should have said, don’t put me as a god. Instead he took it: that speech was perfect. That was his ego, his pride, and the Lord struck him for it. It shows that we shouldn’t desire vainglory or think of ourselves more highly than we ought to.

“And thou his son, O Belshazzar, hast not humbled thine heart, though thou knewest all this; but hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven.” Belshazzar lifted himself up against God, even though he saw what God did to his father. He and his lords, his wives and his concubines drank wine in the vessels of God’s house, and praised the gods of silver and gold, “and the God in whose hand thy breath is, and whose are all thy ways, hast thou not glorified”.

Nebuchadnezzar, when Daniel gave him the dream of the head of gold, got lifted up in his mind and set himself up as a god, and the Lord cast him down: he ran around crazy in the woods. The Lord was saying, don’t exalt yourself; I am the one that lifts people up and takes them down. His son knew that, and still he tested the Lord.

“Brethren, be not children in understanding”: when it comes to understanding, we can’t be children. “Howbeit in malice be ye children.” Why? Because children are quick to forgive and forget. They don’t hold on to grudges. Children don’t have ego, pride and arrogance; that is something we learn as we get older.

“So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.” The key is that we have to forgive from the heart, like a little child. It has to come from the mind: forget about it and let it go. Some brothers and sisters say, I forgive you, but in their mind they hold on to it, and Christ sees that. A lot of people can’t do it, but you have to forgive from the heart.

sense.text: “Then came to him the mother of Zebedee’s children with her sons”, desiring “that these my two sons may sit, the one on thy right hand, and the other on the left, in thy kingdom.” She is asking for them to be the greatest.

“Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of?” When Christ was about to be crucified he asked the Lord to take this cup from him. That cup is affliction, death, being hated. So this shows what being great means: you are going to suffer. When you say, I want to be a great leader, I want to be one of the 144, you had better understand what you are asking for. Every one of the 144 drank of the cup Christ drank of; every one of them suffered and was made perfect through suffering, the same way Christ suffered and was made perfect. They caught hell on this earth.

In order to be a leader of the nation of Israel you have to suffer. You will be hated, and eventually the government is going to come for you. Men have to have that understanding and build themselves up to endure it. Some men become leaders not for love of the people but for vainglory or for money, to be flattered and noticed. That is a hireling: one who is here for a time. Brothers who force themselves up as leaders, whom God did not raise up, will leave the truth when affliction arises for the word’s sake, because they love the glory of men. A leader’s mind has to be programmed that he is going to drink of that same cup. There is no running from it. The bishops and the deacons all know they have to drink of it.

“They say unto him, We are able.”

“Ye shall drink indeed of my cup.” And they did. One of them was killed with the sword by Herod, and the other, John, was exiled on an island; they tried to kill him and he would not die, because the Lord was protecting him. All for the teachings of Christ. Real leaders understand they will suffer. Malcolm X said he was a dead man already. A revolutionary thinks that way: if I keep waking my people up, eventually the devil is coming for me. Every one of us has to drink of that cup and go through that fire; we just have to pray that we can endure.

precepts.why:
This is why Christ says, can you drink of my cup. “For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required.” You want to be a great leader, a deacon, a captain, an officer; you pray for God to bestow much wisdom on you. God requires much more from the leaders, from the 144, than from anyone else. When God gives you a lot of wisdom, he is going to need much more from you. What he reveals to you is to comfort you when you go through bad times, because things are going to get very bad.

“And to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more.” Christ is going to ask much more from the leaders he sets up, and that much more is not just more work in the truth. It is their life.

sense.text:
“Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.” A novice is a beginner, someone who hasn’t been through anything in this truth and lacks experience. When leaders are set up, they cannot be novices, otherwise they are going to be lifted up with pride: they won’t take correction, they get full of themselves, self-absorbed, thinking they are better than everyone, all those characteristics.

Put a novice up as a leader and Satan comes and plays with his ego. He desires vainglory because he was young, never went through certain things, was never corrected. In this truth you have to grow, and growth takes years of going through trials and coming out of them. That is how you learn to deal with certain spirits and to see Satan when he comes. When someone flatters you, saying you are my best deacon, the experienced man says, you freaking Satan, better go from me with that, you ain’t going to get me like that. The novice says, oh yeah, for real.

precepts.why:
This is the bad pride. “Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king”: he was only sixteen, a novice. “And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord.” “And he sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God.” Zechariah was a prophet: God had the right men around this young man to tutor and guide him. “And as long as he sought the Lord, God made him to prosper.” He warred against the Philistines and broke down the walls of Gath, Jabneh and Ashdod; “God helped him”, “and his name spread abroad even to the entering in of Egypt; for he strengthened himself exceedingly.” He became famous, the same way some leaders in here will become famous.

“But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction.” His heart lifted up means he became prideful, highminded. He was being praised, he was winning wars, and he became arrogant: he thought he knew everything and nobody could correct him. It wasn’t there in the beginning, but as time went on it grew; once his counselor was gone, Satan played with him. That is where Paul got it from: not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.

“For he transgressed against the Lord his God, and went into the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar of incense.” He went outside what God commanded him. The priests withstood him: “It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the Lord, but to the priests the sons of Aaron”. “Then Uzziah was wroth, and had a censer in his hand to burn incense.” Pride is not wanting to listen to counsel, not wanting to listen to anybody. “And while he was wroth with the priests, the leprosy even rose up in his forehead before the priests”: that was his judgment. God lifted this king up, he did great things in Israel, and he was lifted up to his own destruction, thinking of himself more highly than he ought.

Here is the good pride, the pride we want to have. Of Jehoshaphat it says, “And his heart was lifted up in the ways of the Lord.” Of Uzziah it said his heart was lifted up to his destruction; of Jehoshaphat it says his heart was lifted up in the ways of the Lord. He wanted to accomplish all the things the Lord told him, to get rid of the idols: “moreover he took away the high places and groves out of Judah.”

sense.text: “Let us go again and visit our brethren in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they do. And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark. But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.” Barnabas wanted to take Mark, his nephew; Barnabas saw something in Mark that Paul didn’t see.

“And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other.” Contention is that argument, that strife. It got so bad that they said, you go your way and do the work there, and I will do the work here. There was pride and ego there. Even Paul and the apostles went through this.

precepts.why: “Only by pride cometh contention.” The contention between Paul and Barnabas only came by pride: pride came on one of them, and that is why the contention took place. “But with the well advised is wisdom.”

Demas had forsaken Paul, “having loved this present world”, and others had gone their ways. “Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee: for he is profitable to me for the ministry.” Whatever contention Paul and Barnabas had over Mark was resolved. Paul now says Mark is profitable, so something changed.

That is why Paul says to endeavour to keep the unity and the bond of peace: people don’t teach on things they never went through. Satan came between him and Barnabas and caused that division. Paul also had to fight pride. He grew up a Pharisee and was very arrogant at times, and the Lord gave him a thorn in the flesh to buffet him, lest he be exalted above measure. The Lord had to humble him, and all of these things Paul had to learn.

sense.text:
“The fear of the Lord is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy”. Arrogance, pride, ego: it is all the same thing, and the Lord hates it.

Ego has a lot of brothers locked up in prison right now: somebody said something and you couldn’t let it go, somebody bumped you and you felt you had to retaliate, your woman told you some dude said something and you went and killed him, because of your ego. Every man has ego, every man has pride, and nobody likes to be disrespected. Those spirits rise up easily in every man, so every last one of us has to examine ourselves and see if it is in us.

Christ said you have to become like a little child: get rid of the ego, get rid of the pride. Christ could have destroyed the whole earth, yet he let the people he created whip him and pluck off his beard. He had to humble himself and take all of that, and it is going to be the same with us. Become like a little child in Christ.
